units.function: Broad route tests for listing and synchronizing Agent Skills across Adapters, canonical references and version pins, Secret-safe configuration resolution, direct Agent creation, managed instruction materialization and hire-approval snapshots.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes authorize and resolve Agent/Company state, use CompanySkillService to canonicalize catalog/version selections, resolve Adapter config through SecretService with user Secrets skipped, delegate list/sync to the active Adapter, persist desired state in Agent adapterConfig and compose AgentService/Instructions/Approval/Issue-link/telemetry flows for creation and hiring.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/Adapter config, desired Skill key or key+versionId, add/remove/replace merge mode, runtime Skill entry/snapshot, beta-Skill setting, user/company Secret context, managed InstructionBundle, pending hire Agent, Approval requestedConfigurationSnapshot and source Issue link.
units.lifecycle: List and sync inspect catalog entries without materializing missing runtime files and skip user-specific Secrets while retaining actor context for company-Secret audit. Sync requires explicit add/remove/replace, canonicalizes references, optionally accepts version pins behind an instance beta flag and persists desired state before Adapter sync. Unknown legacy keys remain visible/removable but are excluded from runtime version selection. Direct creation and hires canonicalize Skills, reject legacy prompt fields, materialize managed default/custom instructions and include desired Skills/config in hire approval payloads.
units.testAssessment: Thirty substantial route cases cover Claude/Codex/ACPX/persistent modes, Secret-resolution options, explicit merge semantics, version gating, stale references, canonicalization, direct create, telemetry role, instruction defaults, legacy rejection and hire approval/source preservation. Missing are real authorization denials and cross-tenant checks, concurrent sync/version conflicts, rollback when persistence or Adapter sync fails, Skill digest/signature/license/trust, permission/tool/data manifests, risk-based approval on post-hire changes, uninstall/rollback, Adapter partial failure, audit events, runtime attestation, malicious Skill content and proof that stale/unverified entries cannot execute through another path. Heavy mocks leave database/filesystem/plugin boundaries unverified.
units.designRationale: Separate desired Skill selection from runtime representation, avoid side effects during reads, preserve backward-compatible stale choices, make destructive replacement explicit and keep Agent creation/approval configuration stable across multiple Adapter ecosystems.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a vendor-neutral Skill/Plugin lifecycle where desired capability, reviewed package version, Connector materialization and effective runtime authority are distinct, auditable states tied to accountable humans and data policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT side-effect-free list/sync preparation, explicit add/remove/replace, canonical references, unresolved-item quarantine, Secret-safe audit context and approval configuration snapshots. Move desired Skills out of vendor Adapter config into a versioned CapabilityAssignment aggregate. Admission requires immutable package digest, provenance/license/signature, declared tools/permissions/data egress and compatibility; activation and every authority-expanding change require risk-based human approval and atomic publish/rollback. Connector-specific materialization remains an Adapter responsibility.
units.responsibilityConflict: A permitted sync can change effective Agent instructions/tools without a new ResponsibilityContract or approval, and a global beta flag substitutes for package trust. versionId is not shown to bind immutable content or license. Stale/unverified keys persist alongside valid desired state. Default instruction bundles encode Paperclip-specific API and operational doctrine, so copying them would couple Company OS behavior and responsibility semantics to a competitor's control plane.
